points.text:
Second board game cafe I tried in philly and what a great experience! 

Best part of the place is the staff. So nice! Lots of good game recommendations. Very attentive and just genuinely nice people. At the end of the night one even brought out some extra cupcakes that they had gotten for their birthday. 

Great beer selection. They even had a couple Cape May Beers on tap which I haven't found elsewhere in the city.

2 star quality also applies to dingy interior and lacking customer service at this location.

points.text: Counter staff wasn't friendly. Food is WAY overpriced, over 6$ for a tiny bagel sandwich with three ingredients. Internet was restricted and unable to connect to any school websites. Will never go to Bennas again!!!!

United by Blue is a nice spot to cool down at after walking through the historic Elfreth's Alley or a fun spot to just drink good coffee at and browse through the clothes collection. 
What you should know:
I. LOCATION 
At the corner of Race & N 2nd St. You'll see apparel through the windows, but I promise there's coffee inside too. 
II. QUALITY
I'm a huge coffee snob, so I always order a black cold brew or Americano

points.text: I love Brodo! Every soup and salad I've ordered has been awesome; so mUch better than Au Bon Pain. Most of the sandwiches have been great too, especially the BLT. questions.question: Where's good for a quiet dinner to take a client?
questions.prepared_answer: Based on the reviews, I'd recommend **Café L'Aube** for a quiet dinner with a client. The review specifically describes it as "my favorite little haven for when I want a bite to eat in a quiet location," and it's praised for "exceptional service and quality food at affordable pricing" — all ideal qualities for a client dinner.

raw.categories: Bars, Restaurants, Chicken Wings, Burgers, Nightlife
raw.text:
Probably will keep this place in mind for a nightcap and dessert. It's a small restaurant/bar. I wanted to have dinner here but their menu was really limited and I ended up eating elsewhere. The dinner menu is less than 10 items but has an Asian twist. They have some good drinks, so I'd probably come back again just for drinks. 

If I were to suggest anything to the owners, it would be to give room on 2 person booths seating for full figured gals/guys (or lower seating perhaps), as those booths

raw.categories: Coffee & Tea, Desserts, Food, French, Creperies, Restaurants
raw.text:
My favorite little haven for when I want a  bite to eat in a quiet location. This place is the reason I want to move in the South Philadelphia area. It's just one of those great little restaurants that give exceptional service and quality food at affordable pricing.

I'd recommend this to anyone interested in trying something different while chatting casually with a friend or a special treat for your significant other. Hint hint!

raw.categories: American (New), French, Restaurants, American (Traditional)
raw.text: Supper is great for brunch and dinner. Very casual yet high quality ingredients. There is even an upstairs area that you can rent out. Right across from whole foods so parking is not a problem

My husband and I had the argula salad and halibut entree.  Both were inventive and very tasteful.  We dine out frequently and my husband commented that this was the best meal he has had in a while. Service was professional and pleasant.  The venue was relaxing; on the small side but tables were adequately spaced.

The only slight negative is that from my seat the line of sight leads into an unslightly  kitchen/service area which slightly detracts from the mood. Would suggest a door or curtain.

Great food and service. On low side: extremely noisy...
For the first timers: They don't serve alcohol. If you want beer or wine, you have to bring it yourself. 
I would give it a 5, but the noise level drove me crazy. I guess it was not the lucky night...few tables around me might have had a contest on who would speak the loudest...

questions.question: Which places are reliably fast for a weekday lunch?
questions.prepared_answer:

**Kitchen Gia** - Described as a "quick place for lunch" where you "select a type of food and go to that counter to order." For salads specifically, you "fill out a form and mark what you want, which limits wait time."

questions.question: Where can I get a good espresso before work?
questions.prepared_answer:
Based on the reviews, here are your best options for a good espresso before work:

**Ben and Betsy's Coffee and Gifts** is your top choice. One reviewer raved it's the "BEST Espresso I've had since Italy," describing the perfect crema with sugar sitting on top before falling to the bottom.

**Green Eggs Café** is also a solid option, offering "great espresso drinks with good food" and "quick service and attentive staff."

**Elixr Coffee** is another good alternative with "really good espresso," though note that it's located in the lobby of a building, so it may be easy to miss.

I'd avoid **Cafe Fulya** — a reviewer specifically went there for espresso but found the staff seemed untrained and the machine appeared out of adjustment.

**La Citadelle** could work "in a hurry" as a backup option, though the reviewer noted it "could be slightly improved."

questions.question: Which places are best for a large group celebration?
questions.prepared_answer:
Based on the reviews, here are the best places for a large group celebration:

**Marrakesh** is a solid option for large groups. According to the review, it's specifically good for celebrations like birthday parties, offers a set menu, friendly staff, belly dancing entertainment, and is BYOB with complimentary mint tea at the end.

**Wax + Wine** is highly recommended for celebrations. The review highlights that it has an amazing atmosphere, super fun employees, and guests leave with unique candles and fond memories.

**Tir na nOg Irish Pub** is great for large parties and groups because they can partition off different sections of the venue to accommodate your group.

**Park Avenue Banquet Hall** is designed for parties with spacious rooms, a nice big dance floor, a square bar, and complimentary decorations. The reviews note it has a pretty all-white room, nice staff, and lots of street parking available.

questions.question: Which places are worth the wait on a weekend?
questions.prepared_answer:
Based on the reviews, here are the places worth the wait on a weekend:

**Day By Day** is an excellent choice for a weekend visit. According to the review, a Sunday visit had "seamless" wait times, and the reviewer praised the attentive service from their waiter Garry. The reviewer also highlighted "great variety of appetizer options and main course dishes."

**Lucy's Hat Shop** is also worth visiting on weekends. The reviewer states they've "been here many times with friends on weekends" and describes it as a "fun place" with "good atmosphere, cool crowd, and good specials" — ideal if you're "looking for a chill casual place to go."

I would **not recommend** **Girard Bruncherie** for a weekend visit. The reviewer explicitly states "Would not recommend a weekend visit," explaining that while the food is "fresh and tasty," the weekend crowds cause service issues and the "nice atmosphere is lost."

As for **Landmark Americana Tap & Grill - University City**, while the food is consistently good, the reviewer specifically mentions "The wait is just something that needs to be worked on," so it may not be the best choice if you want to avoid long waits on weekends.

questions.question: Where would I take out-of-town guests who want something local?
questions.prepared_answer:
For out-of-town guests wanting something local, I'd recommend:

**Dawson Street Pub** - It's described as a "cool local spot" that's "def a locals place, but they're friendly." They offer above average food and lots of live music, which would give your guests an authentic local experience.

**Pinot Boutique** is also a great option if your guests enjoy wine. It specializes in local wines from Pennsylvania, and you can enjoy a meat & cheese tray while sampling local products in a welcoming atmosphere.

Both venues showcase local character and hospitality that would appeal to visitors wanting to experience the area authentically.

questions.question: Which places are good if someone in the group has dietary restrictions?
questions.prepared_answer:
Based on the reviews, here are places good for dietary restrictions:

**[Leziz Turkish Cuisine]** is an excellent choice. The review specifically states they offer "a large family style combination" where "there's literally something for everyone, no matter your tastes or dietary restrictions."

**[Grain Exchange]** is another option. While the reviewer wasn't impressed with the overall food quality, they noted that the staff "were accommodating with my dietary restrictions."

raw.categories: Vegetarian, Middle Eastern, Restaurants, Turkish, Seafood
raw.text:
Try the little-bit-of-everything option for large groups.

We brought in a group of eight people on short notice and ordered one of the large family style combinations. This is a great option because there's literally something for  everyone, no matter your tastes or dietary restrictions.

I loved everything I tried.

I almost traveled to Istanbul, Turkey this year, but that trip fell through. Now that I've been to the Istanbul Lounge, I feel like the universe made it up to me.

questions.question: Where can I get Ethiopian food with vegan options and live jazz on Tuesdays?
questions.prepared_answer:
Based on the reviews provided, I cannot find a restaurant that meets all three of your criteria. 

While **Buna Cafe Philly** is praised for having "many vegan options" and "some of the best Ethiopian food," the reviews don't mention live jazz on Tuesdays.

The reviews also don't contain any information about live jazz on Tuesdays at any of the Ethiopian restaurants listed. I'd recommend contacting these restaurants directly to ask about their Tuesday evening entertainment.

open.text: Interesting little spot for Ethiopian food.  We ate outdoors in the backyard.   Very laid back an comfortable.  You had to go in and place your order at the bar, but that wasn't bad.  Had the veggie combo plate, which filled us up.

open.categories: Ethiopian, Restaurants
open.text: This place is so delicious for authentic Ethiopian food. The man and woman that run the place are very kind. I used to come in person for meals but now a days they take only pick up orders. You can call and place an order. My go to order is the tour of Ethiopia and ask for the recommended veggies to go with it. Very nice portion size with a big injera bread on the side! A west Philly gem for sure!

open.categories: Restaurants, Ethiopian, Dive Bars, Nightlife, Bars
open.text: Had no idea what Ethiopian food was like before this place. Quizzo on Wednesdays! Probably the only reason to go.

open.categories: Restaurants, Ethiopian, Dive Bars, Nightlife, Bars
open.text: This place is cute and the atmosphere was pretty dope, but flavor-wise, it just wasn't there for me. This was my first Ethiopian food experience so maybe I ordered the wrong thing. I would be willing to try again since my friends RAVE about Ethiopian food.

open.categories: Restaurants, Ethiopian, Dive Bars, Nightlife, Bars
open.text: If ya go it's trivia night. Good food not the best Ethiopian in town but a great neighborhood spot. Service was solid and the Trivia guy is serious and knows what he's doing.

open.text: I've eaten a lot of Ethiopian food. I think this is outstanding, although all I've had is the veggie combo, over and over. The injera is just right, the veg dishes are each perfection. My family loves and is always looking for the just-right yetimatim fitfit, and it's great here, almost as crazy-vinegary as we want it.

open_diverse.categories: Nightlife, Music Venues, Beer Bar, Dive Bars, Bars, Whiskey Bars, Arts & Entertainment, Cocktail Bars
open_diverse.text: Love this place. Cute bar, CASH ONLY, you can order Ethiopian food from downstairs and they'll walk it up. The vibe is different on nights where there's music versus not, I prefer music nights a bit more, but of course, there's limited seating when that happens. I still feel a bit weird when I walk through the restaurant to get upstairs, but that's part of the charm!

open_diverse.categories: Vegetarian, Live/Raw Food, Vegan, Restaurants
open_diverse.text: If your looking for meatless or vegetarian options this place is a must! Everything I've had from here is great! Super nice staff ... Food was prepared quick and tastes great!  You have to get the Falafel Sandwich with the works!

open_diverse.categories: Restaurants, Senegalese, African
open_diverse.text: This is my favorite restaurant for African food. Although the restaurant is small, the entire staff are extremely friendly and attentive. And it helps that the food is delicious! I have tried just about everything but my favorites are the Dibi lamb, Yasa fish and potato greens. Be sure to taste the fresh brewed tea full of herbs the owner makes..

open_diverse.categories: American (Traditional), Restaurants, Sandwiches, Caterers, Breakfast & Brunch, Coffee & Tea, Cafes, Event Planning & Services, Burgers, American (New), Vegetarian, Food
open_diverse.text: We are visiting Philly for a few days to catch a baseball game and sightseeing.  Looking for Vegan options for me I found Luna Cafe.  I had the avocado toast with tomatoes which was very good and fresh. I also had the plain potatoes.  My husband had bacon and scrambled eggs.  We had a tour planned for later in the morning so we arrived a few mintes before they opened.  They saw we were there and took our drink order.  Our waitress Maddie was wonderful.

open_diverse.categories: Halal, Restaurants, Middle Eastern
open_diverse.text:
Decent halal / middle eastern food. Shawarma, kafta, kabobs, gyros - and open late night. They also do halal version of American food --- halal pizza and cheesesteaks. Also have vegan options for pizza.

Can order halal food at the counter for Eds Wings too.

Mallu Cafe on Verree just off Bustleton in far Northeast Philly is really a take out Indian joint, with a few tables for those who don't mind the run down decor or aren't aware of the business model employed (like me). Their website was interesting, and showed nice photos of many of their Kerala dishes. Perhaps, I should have been deterred by the sketchy dudes hanging by the front door (even more of them when we left), but they smiled when we approached and invited us in. 

Strange, but no big deal.

We ordered Chicken 65 (spicy chili fried), Avial (mixed veggie coconut curry) and Appam (rice flour fry bread). They arrived in take out containers with plastic forks (?!). The chicken had been deep fried to a very dark brown and delivered without any sauce. Obviously, overcooked by someone who didn't know their own recipe, or hadn't looked at their website, as I had. I returned it to the kitchen. I wanted it done the right way, but that wasn't offered. Rather, they wanted to give us Kerala Chicken Curry. 

Okay. Whatever.

While we waited we sampled the veggie dish. It was cool on top and hot at the base. Microwaved, and no one bothered to see if it was fully recooked. Nope. Further,

Before you ever consider visiting this establishment, please read and consider the type of people that would run a business such as this.

Hi Julie,

I am so sorry to inform you that we will be unable to host your party on Saturday.  I truly apologize for the inconvenience.  We have to make immediate repairs to our kitchen in order to satisfy our insurance company.  We only offer Open Bar Packages upstairs.  Open Bar is not available downstairs.

Thank you for your interest in The Flat Rock Saloon and hopefully you will think of us for your next event.  My sincerest apology.

Amy Talvacchia, Chef

Amy,

The fact that you sent this as an email and didn't have the decency to call directly is both rude and unprofessional.  It's completely unacceptable to cancel two days before the event and not offer any consolation, meaning offering the open bar downstairs or suggesting another venue that might be able to accommodate us. BREAKFAST @ TIFFANY (Diner on the Boulevard)

Happy New Year (2022) Everyone!

My last Yelp of the old year was at this fine establishment in the Great Northeast, Philadelphia. It had been closed an extended period of time for renovations, and the effort appears to have been worthwhile. The facility has a new outer shell and the main dining hall is bright, attractively utilitarian and very clean. Staff from management to servers are courteous and helpful. The menu is a diner's long list of nearly infinite possibilities. 

But, I was there for a New Year's Eve Day breakfast, and while prepared to be tempted, knew what I wanted - French Toast & crisp bacon. There is a long counter along the back wall, and when I arrived it was unoccupied. I sidled down to the third from last spinner, past the last booth, and found myself in the perfect Covidly socially distance spot. No one with ten feet of me. I ordered coffee and my Frenchie. and perused my phone for the latest news while I waited. These days that is always a risky thing to do and expect to keep a good mood, but old habits die hard. (Good riddance 2021!)

review_examples.categories: Bagels, Restaurants, Breakfast & Brunch, Food, Sandwiches, Bakeries
review_examples.text:
Decent enough bagel and friendly service, but it is somewhat amazing that there is so much disparity between one Manhattan Bagel shop and another; this one on Bustleton Avenue in the Russian part of Northeast Philly landing on the lower end of the spectrum. 

Crust not as firm/crisp as others nearby, and far fewer roasted onion flakes attached. Still, more than adequate veggie cream cheese coverage within to help offset the shortcomings. 

Their coffee is strong and holds its own for a breakfast blend. Been sipping it for several hours and it hasn't turned bitter. 

Will certainly do until a real bakery shows up and turns out a Real McCoy bagel, that knows how to bathe well before baking.

review_examples.categories: Donuts, Sandwiches, Soul Food, Food, Coffee & Tea, Restaurants, Chicken Wings
review_examples.text:
Having just had a nice meal nearby, we just so happened to drive by this place. Wondering why the long line outside, I whipped out my handy dandy Yelp app. Saw the awesome reviews and photos and told my companion...STOP the car, turn back, I'm going in. 

Due to COVID-19, only 4 are allowed inside at a time. I was disappointed to find only two flavors available in their glass counter and 3 on their chart. 

Here is what we chose on their limited menu on this Halloween day:
- Cinnamon Brown Sugar
- Strawberry Lavender
- Cookies & Cream

I didn't understand the wait time until I saw them freshly pack up my donuts straight from the fryer. Ooooh, it smelled so good. The paper bag felt warm and I quickly took one out for that first bite. First of all, I am not a donut fan, secondly, donuts that are cake form are usually not my fave because it's too dense & dry. This was anything but. I am totally in love with these donuts. Dare I say it? I like these better than Beiler's.

This place is also famous for their fried chicken as well. I will definitely give it a try on my next visit. Service was prompt and friendly.

Arriving at 3:30, I learned Ban Bamboo closed for two hours on Saturday afternoon and reopened at 4. So, I had a little time to wander along Ridge Avenue and take in the beautiful Spring day and the local color. The street scene was active with outdoor seating at the brewery and many open doors allowing the kitchen aromas to waft out to we pedestrians. Definitely created the aura of being a neighborhood. 

When BB's "Open" sign lit, I went in to discover a small dining area with lovely Buddha shrine front and center, and heavy southeast Asian decor all around. A cafe in Vientiane or Pattaya would look as good. I ordered Tom Kha Soup (veggie), Beef Satay, Red Curry (veggie), Drunken Noodles (chicken), and Kai Soi (beef), to go. It was 40 minutes to readiness, so I continued my exploration of the area while waiting, and thought about what I remembered about Lao and Thai cuisine. 

While both are very regionalized so that there are many distinctions even in different parts of each country. Still, there are a few generalities that hold true.
